key_concepts.concept: Football S&C is preparation for match actions, not generic fitness.
key_concepts.details: The plan should build the ability to accelerate, sprint upright, brake, turn, duel, repeat high-intensity efforts, and stay technically effective late in the match. Running volume, gym work, and recovery all need to map back to football roles and tactical situations.
key_concepts.backend_use: Use football action tags when selecting conditioning, strength, plyometric, and mobility content.

level_implications.beginner: Build broad movement literacy, safe landing, low-volume sprint mechanics, and consistent neuromuscular warm-up habits.
level_implications.intermediate: Progress to role-aware speed, deceleration, repeated-sprint, and unilateral strength blocks.
level_implications.advanced: Use individual match data, sprint exposure, readiness signals, and tactical role demands to tune weekly loading.

key_concepts.concept: Raw distance is not enough to describe soccer load.
key_concepts.details: Match demands change with position, formation, possession state, scoreline, tactical style, opponent level, substitute status, and fatigue. Backend rules should avoid assuming that more total distance means a better or harder football session.
key_concepts.backend_use: Pair workload metrics with role, phase, style, match status, and training objective.

level_implications.beginner: Use simple session categories such as skill, small-sided game, speed, strength, and match.
level_implications.intermediate: Track high-intensity running, accelerations, decelerations, minutes played, and session RPE.
level_implications.advanced: Use individualized speed thresholds and position-specific reference ranges where monitoring exists.

key_concepts.concept: Max-velocity exposure should be built progressively instead of avoided.
key_concepts.details: Hamstring risk rises when players sprint underprepared, but never sprinting leaves them unprepared for wide transition runs, pressing, recovery runs, and through-ball chases. Plans should create regular, controlled exposures to high-speed and near-maximal sprinting when the player is healthy.
key_concepts.backend_use: Create weekly sprint exposure and max-velocity microdose rules with readiness gates.

position_notes.wide_roles: Fullbacks, wingbacks, wingers, and wide forwards need frequent exposure to open-field sprints.
position_notes.center_backs: Even with lower total high-intensity volume, they need sprint reserve for emergency recovery runs.
position_notes.goalkeepers: Need fewer long sprints but still need short accelerations and occasional recovery runs in sweeper actions.

key_concepts.concept: Deceleration is a high-cost load that can hide inside small-sided games.
key_concepts.details: High numbers of hard stops, defensive presses, counterpressing actions, and tight-space turns can produce major eccentric load even when sprint distance is low. A session can be mechanically heavy without looking hard by distance alone.
key_concepts.backend_use: Track and classify deceleration, COD, pressing, and small-sided-game density separately from running distance.
key_concepts.match_week_note: Avoid high volumes of unaccustomed braking and cutting close to match day, especially MD-2 and MD-1.

key_concepts.concept: Change of direction combines perception, braking, body orientation, and re-acceleration.
key_concepts.details: COD training should not be only ladder drills or cone shuttles. Football COD includes reading an opponent, lowering the center of mass, controlling hip-knee-ankle alignment, redirecting force, and executing the next technical action.
key_concepts.backend_use: Link COD exercises to 1v1 defending, dribbling, pressing, and transition drills.

level_implications.beginner: Teach low-speed cuts, landing positions, and braking mechanics before fatigue.
level_implications.intermediate: Add planned and reactive COD with the ball and opponent cues.
level_implications.advanced: Progress to high-speed entry, opponent deception, and match-realistic re-acceleration.

key_concepts.concept: Repeated sprint ability is not just more sprints.
key_concepts.details: Repeated sprint ability depends on max sprint capacity, acceleration strength, aerobic recovery between efforts, phosphocreatine recovery, technical economy, and tactical pacing. Conditioning should mix speed development, high-intensity intervals, small-sided games, and aerobic base work.
key_concepts.backend_use: Separate speed-quality sessions from repeated-sprint conditioning sessions.

key_concepts.concept: Soccer strength needs single-leg, lateral, rotational, and trunk components.
key_concepts.details: Football actions are rarely symmetrical. Sprinting, cutting, tackling, shielding, shooting, landing, and pressing require unilateral force production, pelvis control, trunk stiffness, adductor-abductor coordination, and eccentric braking strength.
key_concepts.backend_use: Prefer soccer-specific strength buckets over a generic lower-body day.

key_concepts.concept: Prevention work is a repeated habit, not a one-off drill.
key_concepts.details: FIFA 11+, Nordic hamstring work, adductor strengthening, calf loading, landing control, and balance work are most useful when integrated consistently and progressed around the match calendar.
key_concepts.backend_use: Create low-friction warm-up and microdose records that can appear repeatedly in plans.

key_concepts.concept: Hamstring, adductor, calf-Achilles, knee, ankle, hip, and trunk risks require different signals.
key_concepts.details: A player can tolerate aerobic running yet still be underprepared for sprinting, adductor squeeze loads, calf stiffness, deep cutting, or contact landings. Readiness logic should not reduce all injury risk to one fatigue score.
key_concepts.backend_use: Use body-region flags and exposure-specific readiness rules.

key_concepts.concept: Match-week planning should protect match quality while maintaining key capacities.
key_concepts.details: The goal is not to remove all training stress before a match, but to place heavy neuromuscular, strength, speed, and tactical load far enough from match day that players can perform. Closer to match day, keep volume lower, maintain sharpness, and avoid novel soreness.
key_concepts.backend_use: Generate MD-minus rules for strength, sprinting, COD, conditioning, recovery, and activation.

key_concepts.concept: Congested periods prioritize availability, recovery, and microdosing.
key_concepts.details: When matches are separated by two to four days, the plan should reduce heavy eccentric volume, limit extensive conditioning for starters, top up non-starters, maintain speed with tiny exposures when safe, and use rotation/readiness rules.
key_concepts.backend_use: Create separate congested-fixture macros instead of applying normal week templates.

key_concepts.concept: Return-to-play should progress from participation to sport to performance.
key_concepts.details: A player who is cleared to train is not automatically ready for full match performance. Backend rules should distinguish return to running, return to team training, return to limited minutes, and return to full match demands.
key_concepts.backend_use: Create RTP records with phase gates, exposures, and minutes progression.

key_concepts.concept: Youth players need growth and maturation safeguards.
key_concepts.details: Rapid growth can temporarily reduce coordination, alter limb leverage, increase tendon and apophyseal sensitivity, and change tolerance to sprinting, jumping, cutting, and contact. Youth programming should account for biological maturity, not only chronological age.
key_concepts.backend_use: Add youth growth-spurt readiness flags and avoid adult-like congested loading for developing players.

key_concepts.concept: Match exposure is not equal across the squad.
key_concepts.details: A substitute who plays 10 minutes and a starter who plays 95 minutes should not receive the same post-match prescription. Non-starters often need controlled top-up conditioning and speed exposure, while starters need recovery and tissue-status checks.
key_concepts.backend_use: Use minutes played, position, and sprint exposure to adjust M+1 and M+2 plans.

key_concepts.concept: Some events require medical removal or referral, not modified training.
key_concepts.details: Suspected concussion, acute severe pain, inability to run normally, marked swelling, neurological symptoms, and rapid worsening symptoms should stop football training decisions and trigger clinical assessment.
key_concepts.backend_use: Create hard-stop readiness rules before generating modified sessions.

technical_models.name: Football action capacity model
technical_models.summary: Organize S&C around the match actions a player must repeatedly express: accelerate, sprint, brake, turn, jump, land, duel, pass or shoot under fatigue, and recover between efforts.

position_notes.center_back: Lower average high-speed volume does not remove the need for sprint reserve and aerial landing capacity.
position_notes.fullback_wingback: High priority for repeated overlaps, recovery runs, accelerations, and eccentric calf-hamstring capacity.
position_notes.central_midfielder: High priority for aerobic repeatability, accelerations, decelerations, and trunk-pelvis stiffness.
position_notes.winger_forward: High priority for max velocity, acceleration, adductor/hamstring resilience, and repeated explosive actions.
position_notes.goalkeeper: High priority for lateral power, short acceleration, landing, trunk stiffness, shoulder robustness, and recovery from dives.

technical_models.name: Acceleration and first-step sprinting
technical_models.summary: Acceleration in football requires horizontal force, trunk angle control, sharp first steps, foot placement under the center of mass, and the ability to accelerate from varied starting postures after perception or technical cues.
programming_examples: resisted accelerations if technique is stable

level_progression.beginner: Teach posture, arm action, and short accelerations with full rest.
level_progression.intermediate: Add varied starts, ball cues, and short resisted or uphill accelerations.
level_progression.advanced: Add reactive starts, duel context, tactical cues, and repeated acceleration clusters with sufficient quality.

technical_models.match_week_rule: Place highest-quality acceleration work early or midweek in a one-match week; use only low-volume sharpness doses at MD-2 or MD-1.

technical_models.name: Max-velocity exposure
technical_models.summary: Healthy players need planned exposure to upright sprinting and high-speed running so hamstrings, calves, and neuromuscular coordination are prepared for match-speed demands.
readiness_gates: no acute hamstring or calf pain
no worsening soreness from prior speed day
avoid maximal exposure during high fatigue
technical_models.match_week_rule: Use a small exposure early-to-midweek if the player did not hit meaningful sprint speed in the match; avoid novel max-speed volume the day before a match.

technical_models.name: Deceleration and braking capacity
technical_models.summary: Deceleration is an eccentric and coordination-heavy skill that requires hip, knee, ankle, calf, trunk, and foot control. It should be taught progressively before high-density pressing, shuttles, and reactive COD work.

level_progression.beginner: Static landings, low-speed stops, and body-position coaching.
level_progression.intermediate: Linear-to-lateral braking, sharper angles, and moderate-density shuttles.
level_progression.advanced: Reactive braking from match speeds, opponent cues, and tactical pressing scenarios.

technical_models.name: Change of direction and reactive agility
technical_models.summary: COD should progress from planned movement mechanics to reactive opponent-led decisions, using the ball and tactical constraints once landing, braking, and trunk control are reliable.
risk_controls: watch knee valgus and trunk collapse
progress entry speed before adding large volume
avoid sharp COD if groin, knee, ankle, or Achilles symptoms are active

technical_models.name: Repeated sprint and high-intensity running model
technical_models.summary: Repeated sprint ability depends on sprint quality, acceleration strength, aerobic recovery, high-intensity running tolerance, and tactical pacing. It should not be developed only with exhaustive shuttles.
technical_models.programming_note: Separate pure speed quality days from repeated sprint conditioning days when possible, because the desired adaptations and fatigue cost differ.

technical_models.name: Unilateral strength and pelvis control
technical_models.summary: Football strength should include split-squat, single-leg hinge, step-down, lateral lunge, Copenhagen, calf, and anti-rotation patterns to support sprinting, cutting, kicking, shielding, and landing.

progression.intermediate: External load, range, and lateral-plane work.
progression.advanced: Heavy unilateral strength, high-velocity intent, integrated plyometrics, and position-specific force angles.

technical_models.name: Hamstring resilience model
technical_models.summary: Hamstring preparation should combine progressive high-speed running, eccentric knee-flexor strength, hip-extension strength, lumbopelvic control, fatigue management, and return-to-sprint criteria after injury.
technical_models.match_week_rule: Heavy eccentric hamstring work is best placed far enough from match day to avoid soreness; near match day, use low-volume activation or isometrics when appropriate.

technical_models.name: Adductor and groin durability model
technical_models.summary: Groin durability requires adductor strength, controlled kicking and cutting exposure, hip range, trunk-pelvis control, and symptom-aware progressions. Copenhagen adduction is a central but not exclusive tool.
risk_controls: avoid sudden increases in shooting or crossing volume
reduce lateral COD if adductor pain increases
distinguish adductor-related symptoms from hip, iliopsoas, inguinal, or pubic symptoms

technical_models.name: Calf and Achilles capacity model
technical_models.summary: Calf and Achilles preparation should build soleus and gastrocnemius strength, tendon load tolerance, ankle stiffness, pogo capacity, sprint tolerance, and progressive plyometric exposure.

technical_models.name: Ankle-knee-hip control model
technical_models.summary: Lower-limb control should connect foot/ankle proprioception, knee alignment, hip control, pelvis stability, and trunk position during cuts, landings, tackles, and repeated technical actions.
programming_examples: hip abduction and external rotation work

technical_models.name: Trunk stiffness and force transfer
technical_models.summary: Trunk stiffness helps transfer force during sprinting, duels, shielding, shooting, change of direction, and landing. It should include anti-extension, anti-rotation, lateral chain, and dynamic bracing rather than only sit-ups.

position_notes.defenders: Need trunk stiffness for duels, aerial contests, and tackles.
position_notes.midfielders: Need repeated bracing while scanning, receiving, and changing direction under contact.
position_notes.attackers: Need trunk control during sprinting, cutting, shooting, and riding challenges.
position_notes.goalkeepers: Need trunk stiffness for diving, landing, and rapid recovery to set position.

technical_models.name: Standard one-match microcycle model
technical_models.summary: For a seven-day week with one match, use post-match recovery, then place the main neuromuscular, strength, speed, tactical, and conditioning work early or midweek, then taper volume while keeping sharpness.

template.M_plus_1: Recovery for starters; controlled top-up for non-starters based on minutes and exposure.
template.MD_minus_4_or_3: Main strength, speed exposure, high-intensity running, or larger tactical load depending on team calendar.
template.MD_minus_2: Moderate tactical speed and set-piece work; reduce volume and avoid novel eccentric soreness.
template.MD_minus_1: Activation, mobility, rehearsal, short accelerations, and low-volume technical/tactical clarity.
template.match_day: Warm-up, performance, and post-match cooldown/recovery logging.

technical_models.name: Congested fixture model
technical_models.summary: When there are two matches in a week or two to four days between matches, reduce heavy training volume for likely starters, maintain capacity with microdoses, top up non-starters, and use readiness plus rotation decisions.

template.starters: Recovery, tissue checks, tactical rehearsal, short activation, and medical/readiness decisions.
template.non_starters: Controlled top-up running, strength, and speed work if freshness and schedule allow.
template.returning_players: Do not use congested fixtures as the first full exposure to match demands after injury.

technical_models.name: Return-to-run and return-to-play continuum
technical_models.summary: Progress from symptom-controlled mobility and strength to linear running, high-speed running, sprinting, cutting, football drills, non-contact team training, contact/team training, limited match minutes, and full performance.
phase_gates: high-speed and sprint exposure restored where relevant

technical_models.name: Youth growth and maturation model
technical_models.summary: Youth planning should adjust load around rapid growth, coordination changes, school stress, tournament congestion, sleep, nutrition, and chronological versus biological age.
risk_flags: new heel, knee, hip, or groin pain
technical_models.programming_response: Lower peak intensity and volume when symptoms or rapid growth flags appear, preserve movement skill, and progress strength with excellent technique.

tactical_rules.situation: High press, counterpress, or repeated front-foot defending
tactical_rules.rule: A team that presses high needs players prepared for repeated accelerations, hard decelerations, re-accelerations, and short recovery windows.
tactical_rules.training_implication: Do not prescribe high-density pressing games on heavy legs without considering deceleration and adductor/calf load; use fewer reps or larger rests when readiness is low.

position_specific_notes.forwards: Need repeated curved accelerations and braking to screen passing lanes.
position_specific_notes.midfielders: Need second-wave pressure, cover, and re-press capacity.
position_specific_notes.defenders: Need connected line height and recovery sprint reserve behind the press.

tactical_rules.situation: Overlaps, underlaps, recovery runs, counterattacks, and balls into channels
tactical_rules.rule: Wide players need regular max-velocity and high-speed running exposure because their decisive actions often occur over larger spaces.
tactical_rules.training_implication: Fullbacks, wingbacks, wingers, and wide forwards should not rely only on small-sided games for speed preparation.

tactical_rules.situation: Central midfield roles in possession, out of possession, and transition
tactical_rules.rule: Central midfielders need high repeatability across accelerations, decelerations, support angles, pressing support, and technical actions under fatigue.
tactical_rules.training_implication: Blend aerobic base, high-intensity intervals, small-sided games, trunk stiffness, and unilateral strength rather than only sprint work.

tactical_rules.situation: High defensive line, defending through balls, covering wide channels
tactical_rules.rule: Center backs may record lower sprint volume than wide roles, but their sprints are often high consequence and must be trained.
tactical_rules.training_implication: Include occasional recovery-run and opening-up sprint work, plus hamstring, calf, trunk, landing, and duel capacity.

tactical_rules.situation: Fast break, transition attack, direct play, and repeated runs in behind
tactical_rules.rule: Counterattack training can create meaningful high-speed and sprint load even if the session is tactical.
tactical_rules.training_implication: Count transition games and run-in-behind patterns toward weekly speed exposure and hamstring/calf load.

tactical_rules.situation: Small-sided games, rondos with pressing, 1v1 channels, and tight possession games
tactical_rules.rule: Tight-space training often increases accelerations, decelerations, lateral pushes, and cutting even when total distance and sprint distance are modest.
tactical_rules.training_implication: Use lower duration or longer rest if adductor, ankle, knee, or Achilles symptoms are present.

tactical_rules.situation: Corners, free kicks, aerial duels, and goalkeeper claiming practice
tactical_rules.rule: Set-piece practice is not purely tactical; it can accumulate jumping, contact, neck/trunk bracing, and landing load.
tactical_rules.training_implication: Manage volume for players with ankle, knee, Achilles, groin, or back issues, and avoid large new aerial-contact volume late in the week.

tactical_rules.situation: Post-match training for substitutes and unused players
tactical_rules.rule: Non-starters should receive controlled top-up work based on what they missed: speed, high-intensity running, accelerations/decelerations, or technical/tactical minutes.
tactical_rules.training_implication: Do not prescribe the same top-up to a winger who missed sprint exposure and a central midfielder who needs aerobic repeatability.

tactical_rules.situation: Player returning from injury to team training
tactical_rules.rule: RTP should include the football situations that create the player's position-specific loads, not only generic running clearance.
tactical_rules.training_implication: A returning winger needs sprint-in-behind and braking exposure; a midfielder needs repeat decel and contact support actions; a center back needs recovery sprints, jumps, and duels.

physical_demands.why_it_matters: Most football sprints begin from low speed or a tactical cue, and early acceleration often decides pressing, loose-ball races, first touches, and 1v1 separation.
assessment_or_monitoring: session acceleration counts where tracking exists

level_implications.beginner: Use short distances, full rest, and simple technique cues.
level_implications.intermediate: Add varied starting postures and ball or opponent cues.
level_implications.advanced: Use position-specific starts, resisted options, and tactical triggers without excessive volume.

physical_demands.demand: Max velocity and high-speed running exposure
physical_demands.why_it_matters: Open-field runs, channel runs, recovery runs, and runs in behind require players to tolerate high-speed mechanics and hamstring/calf loads.
assessment_or_monitoring: peak speed relative to known max

level_implications.beginner: Use progressive strides and relaxed mechanics before true max speed.
level_implications.intermediate: Add controlled sprint exposures weekly when healthy.
level_implications.advanced: Use individual speed thresholds and match-data gaps to decide exposure.

physical_demands.why_it_matters: Pressing, defending, dribbling, and transition actions require players to stop or slow sharply without losing alignment or control.

level_implications.beginner: Teach low-speed stops, soft knees, and trunk control.
level_implications.intermediate: Add faster entries and lateral stops.
level_implications.advanced: Use reactive, tactical, and opponent-led braking.

physical_demands.demand: Change of direction and reactive agility
physical_demands.why_it_matters: Football COD occurs in response to opponents, passes, dribbles, pressing cues, and loose balls, and it stresses adductors, knees, ankles, hips, and trunk control.
assessment_or_monitoring: knee valgus or trunk collapse observations

level_implications.beginner: Planned cuts before reactive cuts.
level_implications.intermediate: Ball and defender cues.
level_implications.advanced: High-speed entry and position-specific deception.

physical_demands.why_it_matters: Players must repeat explosive efforts with incomplete recovery during pressing, transitions, counterattacks, and recovery defending.

level_implications.beginner: Build running tolerance and basic speed first.
level_implications.intermediate: Add repeated sprint sets with full technical quality.
level_implications.advanced: Use tactical repeated-sprint scenarios and role-specific work-rest ratios.

physical_demands.why_it_matters: Aerobic fitness supports repeated high-intensity efforts, technical concentration, recovery between sprints, and tolerance of dense training weeks.
assessment_or_monitoring: ability to recover between high-intensity bouts

level_implications.beginner: Use games, tempo intervals, and general running exposure.
level_implications.intermediate: Use mixed aerobic intervals and small-sided games.
level_implications.advanced: Individualize high-intensity intervals by role, season phase, and match minutes.

physical_demands.why_it_matters: High-intensity running bridges aerobic work and sprinting and is common in support runs, pressing, recovery, and transition play.

level_implications.beginner: Use simple interval games and avoid large spikes.
level_implications.intermediate: Progress intervals and football-specific running patterns.
level_implications.advanced: Use role-specific speed zones and tactical constraints.

physical_demands.why_it_matters: Single-leg strength supports sprinting, cutting, jumping, shooting, shielding, and deceleration while reducing asymmetry and control issues.

level_implications.beginner: Control bodyweight and tempo.
level_implications.intermediate: Add load and range of motion.
level_implications.advanced: Use heavy, high-velocity, and lateral-plane progressions.

physical_demands.why_it_matters: Hamstrings face high loads during sprinting and late swing-phase control, with high burden in football injury surveillance.

level_implications.beginner: Use low-volume bridge, slider, and hinge progressions.
level_implications.intermediate: Add Nordic hamstring progressions and sprint exposure.
level_implications.advanced: Use eccentric strength, sprint mechanics, and individualized sprint exposure based on match data.

physical_demands.why_it_matters: Cutting, lateral pushing, tackling, kicking, shooting, and crossing load the adductors and groin complex.

level_implications.beginner: Use adductor isometrics and controlled lateral movement.
level_implications.intermediate: Progress Copenhagen variations and lateral strength.
level_implications.advanced: Integrate heavy lateral work, kicking volume management, and high-speed COD exposure.

physical_demands.demand: Calf, Achilles, and ankle stiffness capacity
physical_demands.why_it_matters: Repeated accelerations, sprinting, jumping, landings, and changes of direction demand calf strength and Achilles tendon load tolerance.
role_emphasis: players returning from calf or Achilles symptoms

level_implications.beginner: Build calf strength and balance before high plyometric volume.
level_implications.intermediate: Add pogos, skips, and sprint progression.
level_implications.advanced: Use high-stiffness plyometrics and max-speed exposure with symptom gates.

physical_demands.why_it_matters: Landing, cutting, tackling, and reactive agility require coordinated lower-limb alignment and trunk control, especially under fatigue.
role_emphasis: female and adolescent players as a high-priority education group

level_implications.beginner: Master landing and balance patterns.
level_implications.intermediate: Add loaded unilateral and lateral tasks.
level_implications.advanced: Integrate high-speed reactive COD and contact scenarios.

physical_demands.why_it_matters: Trunk control supports sprint mechanics, duels, shooting, shielding, tackling, cutting, and goalkeeper dives.

level_implications.beginner: Basic bracing and anti-extension.
level_implications.intermediate: Anti-rotation, carries, and lateral-chain strength.
level_implications.advanced: Reactive trunk stiffness during contact, sprinting, and striking.

physical_demands.why_it_matters: Headers, set pieces, tackles, blocks, goalkeeper claims, and duels create contact and landing demands that standard running load does not capture.

level_implications.beginner: Teach landing mechanics and safe body positions.
level_implications.intermediate: Add controlled aerial duels and contact preparation.
level_implications.advanced: Integrate set-piece, contested landing, and tactical duel load with recovery planning.

physical_demands.demand: Goalkeeper explosive lateral, dive, and recovery demand
physical_demands.why_it_matters: Goalkeepers require explosive lateral power, repeated set positions, diving and landing tolerance, short recovery movements, and upper-limb/trunk robustness.

level_implications.beginner: Teach set position, landing, and low-height diving safely.
level_implications.intermediate: Add lateral power, plyometrics, and repeated save sequences.
level_implications.advanced: Integrate explosive goalkeeper actions with distribution, crosses, and congested match recovery.

physical_demands.demand: Youth growth, coordination, and maturation capacity
physical_demands.why_it_matters: Youth athletes can temporarily lose coordination and tissue tolerance during rapid growth, increasing risk during sprinting, cutting, jumping, and congested tournaments.

level_implications.beginner: Keep movement skill broad and avoid adult volumes.
level_implications.intermediate: Progress strength and speed while watching growth-spurt flags.
level_implications.advanced: Individualize by biological maturity, not only team age group.

injury_or_load_risks.risk: Hamstring risk from sprint underexposure or sudden high-speed spike
injury_or_load_risks.adjustment_rule: Avoid both sudden maximal sprint spikes and long periods with no high-speed exposure; use graded sprint exposure when pain-free and medically cleared.
avoid: new maximal sprint volume on MD-1
repeated high-speed running while posterior thigh pain is escalating
clearing RTP based only on jogging tolerance

signals: pain after shooting or crossing volume
injury_or_load_risks.adjustment_rule: Reduce lateral COD, aggressive kicking volume, and high-load Copenhagen work during symptom flares; keep tolerable isometrics and progressive strengthening.
avoid: unmonitored increase in shooting/crossing volume
fatigued lateral shuttles with groin pain
ignoring hip-related or inguinal-related symptoms

injury_or_load_risks.risk: Knee and ACL risk during cutting, landing, deceleration, and contact perturbations
injury_or_load_risks.adjustment_rule: Prioritize movement-quality gates, strength symmetry, hop quality, progressive COD, and medical criteria before full training or matches.
avoid: fatigued reactive cutting before basic landing control
returning to full contact after swelling or instability
using time since injury as the only RTP criterion

injury_or_load_risks.risk: Ankle sprain risk and poor proprioception
injury_or_load_risks.adjustment_rule: Use balance, proprioception, calf strength, hop-control, and progressive COD before open reactive play.
avoid: early return to chaotic small-sided games without landing control
sharp COD with swelling or instability
ignoring repeated ankle rolls

injury_or_load_risks.risk: Calf strain or Achilles tendon overload from sprint, plyometric, or surface-load spikes
injury_or_load_risks.adjustment_rule: Reduce plyometric and max-speed volume during symptom escalation; keep tolerable isometrics or heavy-slow resistance under clinical guidance and progress tendon load gradually.
avoid: sudden pogo or sprint volume increases
max-velocity work when tendon pain worsens during warm-up
dense calf loading before matches

injury_or_load_risks.risk: Excessive eccentric soreness from deceleration and COD load
signals: high deceleration count where tracking exists
injury_or_load_risks.adjustment_rule: Move dense deceleration work away from match day; reduce shuttle density and tight-space game duration when soreness or fixture congestion is high.
avoid: large COD volume at MD-1
new aggressive braking drills during tournament weeks
conditioning only through maximal shuttles

injury_or_load_risks.risk: Injury risk from workload spikes or low chronic preparation
injury_or_load_risks.adjustment_rule: Progress load gradually and use the player's recent exposure history before assigning full football conditioning or match minutes.
avoid: full match demand after a quiet training block
large top-up session after long inactivity
rapidly stacking speed, COD, and match minutes

injury_or_load_risks.adjustment_rule: Prioritize recovery, tactical clarity, activation, and rotation; use non-starter top-ups rather than loading the whole squad equally.
avoid: normal heavy gym week between matches
large high-intensity top-up for starters
first RTP match as full minutes during congestion

injury_or_load_risks.risk: Returning to football before match-specific exposure is restored
signals: can jog but has not sprinted
can train non-contact but not cut/contact
injury_or_load_risks.adjustment_rule: Use phase-based RTP gates and progress from running to football-specific exposure to controlled minutes before full performance.
avoid: full match based on pain-free jogging
clearing a winger without sprint-in-behind exposure
clearing a center back without jumps, duels, and recovery sprint exposure

injury_or_load_risks.risk: Beginner overconditioning and poor movement quality under fatigue
injury_or_load_risks.adjustment_rule: Use short quality blocks, movement education, games, and gradual conditioning; do not use exhaustive fitness tests as the main development method.
avoid: maximal repeated sprint sessions without speed foundation
large plyometric volumes
fatigue-first COD drills

injury_or_load_risks.risk: Youth growth and maturation load sensitivity
signals: new heel, knee, hip, groin, or back pain
injury_or_load_risks.adjustment_rule: Reduce peak intensity or volume when growth-pain flags appear; prioritize movement quality, strength technique, sleep, and medical referral if symptoms persist.
avoid: adult-style congested match load
punishing loss of coordination during growth
ignoring apophyseal pain

injury_or_load_risks.risk: Higher-priority knee-control education for female and adolescent players
injury_or_load_risks.adjustment_rule: Make neuromuscular warm-ups, landing control, hip-trunk strength, and progressive COD a default part of training rather than an optional add-on.
avoid: high-fatigue cutting without mechanics
skipping warm-up prevention work
return to full play after swelling or instability

injury_or_load_risks.risk: Goalkeeper landing, shoulder, wrist, trunk, and hip load
injury_or_load_risks.adjustment_rule: Manage dive volume, landing progressions, lateral power, trunk bracing, and recovery during congested weeks.
avoid: large new dive volume after layoff
hard-ground repeated dives late in match week
ignoring upper-limb pain after saves

injury_or_load_risks.adjustment_rule: Remove from football activity and follow medical assessment and graduated return protocols; do not treat symptoms as ordinary fatigue.
avoid: same-day return after suspected concussion
conditioning test to prove readiness
masking symptoms to continue training

injury_or_load_risks.risk: Recovery deficit from poor sleep, travel, low energy intake, or school/work stress
injury_or_load_risks.adjustment_rule: Lower non-essential volume, prioritize nutrition/sleep/recovery, and avoid adding new neuromuscular stress when recovery capacity is low.
avoid: punitive extra conditioning
maximal tests on poor recovery
heavy eccentric work after travel and sleep loss

injury_or_load_risks.risk: Surface, footwear, and weather changes altering tissue load
signals: change from grass to turf or hard ground
injury_or_load_risks.adjustment_rule: Reduce novel sprint, plyometric, and COD volume when surface or footwear changes substantially, especially for calf, Achilles, ankle, and groin-sensitive players.
avoid: new boots plus high-volume sprint/COD session
hard-ground plyometrics after calf symptoms
ignoring slipping during high-speed cuts

training_implications.rule: Progress football S&C from movement quality and exposure literacy to role-specific capacity and then individualized monitoring.
training_implications.beginner: FIFA 11+ style warm-up habits, landing and balance, low-volume acceleration, basic strength, aerobic games, and simple recovery habits.
training_implications.intermediate: Role-aware speed, HIR, COD, unilateral strength, hamstring/adductor/calf durability, and match-week load placement.
training_implications.advanced: Individualized thresholds, sprint exposure targets, GPS/RPE/wellness integration, injury-history rules, rotation, and RTP phase gates.

training_implications.rule: Place the heaviest lower-body strength and eccentric work far enough from match day to avoid soreness and neuromuscular fatigue.

match_week_rules.MD_minus_4_or_3: Best window for heavier strength if the prior match recovery is adequate.
match_week_rules.MD_minus_2: Use moderate or reduced-volume strength, mostly activation, power, or low-soreness work.
match_week_rules.MD_minus_1: Avoid heavy lower-body eccentric strength; use activation and mobility only.
match_week_rules.M_plus_1: Starters recover; non-starters may do top-up strength if not near the next match.

training_implications.congested_fixture_adjustment: Use maintenance microdoses or skip heavy strength for likely starters; preserve small upper-body/core or low-soreness isometrics if needed.

training_implications.rule: Healthy players should keep some speed exposure in the week, but dose it according to match exposure, readiness, and days to the next match.

match_week_rules.MD_minus_4_or_3: Quality sprint or high-speed exposure window if needed.
match_week_rules.MD_minus_2: Low-volume accelerations or fast strides if fresh.
match_week_rules.MD_minus_1: Very small activation only; no new max-speed volume.
match_week_rules.M_plus_1_or_2: Use match data to decide if non-starters need top-up high-speed exposure.

training_implications.congested_fixture_adjustment: For starters, only tiny speed touches if freshness allows; for non-starters, controlled top-up may be needed.

training_implications.rule: High-density deceleration and COD work should usually be earlier than MD-2 in a standard week and reduced during congestion.

match_week_rules.MD_minus_4_or_3: Main COD, pressing, and tight-space load window.
match_week_rules.MD_minus_2: Reduced volume; tactical clarity without large fatigue.
match_week_rules.MD_minus_1: Minimal sharpness and rehearsed patterns only.
match_week_rules.M_plus_1: Check soreness from match decelerations before adding shuttles or small-sided games.

training_implications.congested_fixture_adjustment: Avoid large shuttle or tight-space games for starters; use tactical walk-through, activation, and low-volume technical speed.

training_implications.rule: Strength priorities should reflect football role demands rather than one generic soccer template.

position_specific_notes.center_back: Trunk stiffness, landing/aerial capacity, hamstring sprint reserve, adductor strength, and contact robustness.
position_specific_notes.fullback_wingback: Repeated acceleration, max-speed exposure, calf/Achilles capacity, hamstring resilience, and unilateral lateral strength.
position_specific_notes.defensive_midfielder: Deceleration, trunk stiffness, adductor strength, hip control, and repeatability for duels and cover.
position_specific_notes.central_midfielder: Aerobic base, repeated accelerations/decelerations, unilateral strength, and pelvis/trunk control.
position_specific_notes.attacking_midfielder: COD, acceleration, trunk stiffness under contact, adductor/kicking volume tolerance.
position_specific_notes.winger_wide_forward: Max velocity, repeated sprint ability, adductor and hamstring resilience, calf stiffness, and braking after dribbles.
position_specific_notes.striker_center_forward: Acceleration, sprint-in-behind exposure, hamstring/adductor capacity, trunk bracing, and aerial/contact landing.
position_specific_notes.goalkeeper: Lateral power, dive landing, trunk stiffness, short acceleration, shoulder/wrist robustness, and hip/groin control.

training_implications.rule: Previous injury changes the default exercise selection, volume, and progression gates.

adjustments.hamstring_history: Require graded sprint exposure and eccentric hamstring progression before repeated max-speed work.
adjustments.groin_history: Control adductor, cutting, and kicking volume; progress Copenhagen and lateral strength carefully.
adjustments.acl_history: Use criteria-based strength, hop, landing, COD, and contact progressions before full play.
adjustments.ankle_history: Use balance, calf strength, landing, and bracing/taping decisions before chaotic play.
adjustments.achilles_history: Monitor morning stiffness and pain response; progress plyometrics and sprinting gradually.

training_implications.rule: Split the squad into starters, partial-minute players, and non-starters after each match.
training_implications.starter_plan: Recovery, mobility, wellness check, medical flags, tactical rehearsal, and low-volume activation.
training_implications.partial_minutes_plan: Individual top-up based on missed running, sprint, or COD exposure and next-match likelihood.
training_implications.non_starter_plan: Controlled top-up running, strength, and speed exposure, but avoid making the top-up harder than match load.

training_implications.rule: Youth football S&C should protect long-term development while building strength, movement skill, and football-specific speed gradually.
training_implications.beginner: Use fun movement variety, balance, landing, basic strength, small accelerations, and no adult-style conditioning punishment.
training_implications.intermediate: Monitor growth and pain; progress sprinting, COD, and strength with technique gates.
training_implications.advanced: Individualize by maturity, school load, tournament congestion, and injury history; do not use professional adult microcycles blindly.

training_implications.rule: Return-to-run should progress from walk-jog to continuous running, tempo, high-intensity running, sprinting, COD, football drills, and match minutes.

position_specific_notes.wide_roles: Need open-field sprinting before full match return.
position_specific_notes.midfielders: Need repeat deceleration and support-run tolerance.
position_specific_notes.defenders: Need recovery sprints, jumps, tackles, and duel exposure.
position_specific_notes.goalkeepers: Need dive, landing, lateral push-off, and distribution tolerance.

training_implications.rule: Select conditioning by adaptation goal: aerobic base, high-intensity running, repeated sprint ability, speed quality, or tactical density.

examples.aerobic_base: Extensive tempo, longer intervals, or larger-sided games.
examples.high_intensity_running: Intervals or transition games with controlled rest.
examples.repeated_sprint: Short sprint clusters with incomplete but planned recovery.
examples.tactical_density: Small-sided games with constraints and monitored mechanical load.

training_implications.rule: Do not use maximal fitness testing or exhaustive conditioning as a default response to poor match performance.
training_implications.rationale: Poor performance may reflect tactical role, technical execution, fatigue, recovery, confidence, or match context. Fitness tests should have a clear purpose and be placed away from important matches.

training_implications.rule: Use a traffic-light readiness system before high-risk football loads.
training_implications.green: No red flags, normal soreness, good sleep/recovery, no escalating pain; planned training can proceed.
training_implications.amber: Elevated soreness, low sleep, minor symptoms, recent load jump, or congestion; reduce volume, intensity, COD, sprint, or eccentric work.
training_implications.red: Acute injury, suspected concussion, swelling, instability, severe pain, neurological symptoms, or worsening tendon/muscle pain; stop and refer to medical assessment.

backend_records_to_create.name: Acceleration and first 10 m demand
backend_records_to_create.summary: Short acceleration capacity for pressing, first touches, loose balls, and separation.

level_implications.beginner: Technique, posture, and low-volume starts.
level_implications.intermediate: Varied starts and ball cues.
level_implications.advanced: Reactive, tactical, and position-specific starts.

position_notes: forwards and pressers need repeated starts

backend_records_to_create.name: Max velocity and high-speed exposure
backend_records_to_create.summary: Planned high-speed and near-max sprint exposure for match readiness and hamstring/calf preparation.

level_implications.beginner: Relaxed strides and progressive mechanics.
level_implications.intermediate: Weekly controlled sprint exposure when healthy.
level_implications.advanced: Individualized thresholds and exposure based on match data.

backend_records_to_create.match_week_rule: Dose early-to-midweek in normal weeks; use small activation only close to match day.

backend_records_to_create.name: Deceleration and change-of-direction load
backend_records_to_create.summary: Mechanical load from braking, cutting, pressing, dribbling, and tight-space football.

level_implications.beginner: Low-speed braking and landing control.
level_implications.intermediate: Faster planned COD and lateral strength.
level_implications.advanced: Reactive COD and match-speed pressing/cutting.

backend_records_to_create.match_week_rule: Avoid large novel COD volume at MD-2 or MD-1.

backend_records_to_create.name: Repeated sprint ability
backend_records_to_create.summary: Capacity to reproduce explosive efforts with incomplete recovery.

level_implications.beginner: Develop general running tolerance and basic speed.
level_implications.intermediate: Add repeated sprint sets with quality control.
level_implications.advanced: Use role-specific work-rest and tactical repeated-sprint scenarios.

backend_records_to_create.name: Aerobic base and high-intensity running
backend_records_to_create.summary: Aerobic and high-intensity running capacity supporting repeatability, recovery, and late-game output.

level_implications.beginner: Games and simple intervals.
level_implications.intermediate: Intervals, larger games, and session RPE.
level_implications.advanced: Individualized role-specific running and tactical conditioning.

backend_records_to_create.name: Unilateral lower-body strength
backend_records_to_create.summary: Single-leg strength for sprinting, cutting, shooting, landing, and duels.

level_implications.beginner: Bodyweight control and slow eccentrics.
level_implications.intermediate: Loaded split squats, hinges, lateral lunges, step-downs.
level_implications.advanced: Heavy and high-velocity unilateral strength plus plyometric transfer.

backend_records_to_create.name: Hamstring resilience
backend_records_to_create.summary: Eccentric hamstring strength plus progressive sprint exposure and lumbopelvic control.

level_implications.beginner: Bridge, slider, hinge basics.
level_implications.intermediate: Nordic progressions and controlled sprinting.
level_implications.advanced: Integrated eccentric strength, sprint exposure, and return-to-sprint monitoring.

backend_records_to_create.name: Adductor and groin durability
backend_records_to_create.summary: Adductor strength, hip control, cutting tolerance, and kicking-volume management.

level_implications.beginner: Adductor isometrics and controlled lateral movement.
level_implications.intermediate: Short-to-long lever Copenhagen and lateral strength.
level_implications.advanced: High-speed COD, kicking volume tolerance, and integrated lateral power.

backend_records_to_create.name: Calf and Achilles capacity
backend_records_to_create.summary: Calf strength, tendon load tolerance, ankle stiffness, and graded plyometric/sprint exposure.

level_implications.beginner: Calf strength and balance.
level_implications.intermediate: Pogos, skips, and sprint progression.
level_implications.advanced: High-stiffness plyometrics and max-speed exposure with symptom gates.

backend_records_to_create.name: Ankle, knee, and hip control
backend_records_to_create.summary: Lower-limb alignment and control during landing, cutting, tackling, and reactive football actions.

level_implications.beginner: Balance and landing mechanics.
level_implications.intermediate: Loaded single-leg and lateral movement.
level_implications.advanced: Reactive COD, contact perturbation, and match-specific landing.

backend_records_to_create.name: Trunk stiffness and bracing
backend_records_to_create.summary: Anti-extension, anti-rotation, lateral-chain, and bracing capacity for sprinting, duels, shooting, COD, and goalkeeping.

level_implications.beginner: Basic bracing patterns.
level_implications.intermediate: Anti-rotation, side-chain, and carries.
level_implications.advanced: Reactive bracing under contact and speed.

backend_records_to_create.name: Hamstring sprint-load risk rule
backend_records_to_create.recommended_adjustment: Reduce max sprint volume during symptoms; rebuild graded sprint exposure and eccentric hamstring capacity before full sprint or match load.

backend_records_to_create.name: Groin and adductor risk rule
backend_records_to_create.recommended_adjustment: Limit aggressive COD and kicking; use tolerable adductor isometrics and progressive Copenhagen/lateral strength.
hard_stop_conditions: unclear hip or inguinal symptoms needing clinical review

backend_records_to_create.name: Knee and ACL control risk rule
backend_records_to_create.recommended_adjustment: Require clinical review for swelling/instability; otherwise regress to strength, landing, and planned COD before reactive football.
hard_stop_conditions: unable to cut or land without pain

backend_records_to_create.name: Ankle sprain and proprioception risk rule
backend_records_to_create.recommended_adjustment: Use balance, calf strength, hop-control, taping/bracing if medically recommended, and progressive COD before open play.

backend_records_to_create.name: Calf and Achilles tendon risk rule
backend_records_to_create.recommended_adjustment: Reduce sprint, plyometric, and hard-surface volume; maintain tolerable calf isometrics or heavy-slow resistance under clinical guidance.

backend_records_to_create.name: Suspected concussion hard-stop rule
backend_records_to_create.recommended_adjustment: Remove from football activity and refer for medical assessment and graduated return guidance.
hard_stop_conditions: any suspected concussion symptom after head impact

backend_records_to_create.name: Youth growth and maturation risk rule
backend_records_to_create.recommended_adjustment: Reduce high-impact and high-intensity volume, preserve movement quality, avoid punishment conditioning, and seek clinical review if pain persists.

backend_records_to_create.name: Standard one-match week structure
backend_records_to_create.summary: Use recovery after the match, main load early or midweek, then taper volume while preserving tactical sharpness.

rules.M_plus_1: Recovery for starters; individualized top-up for non-starters.
rules.MD_minus_4_or_3: Main strength, speed, HIR, COD, or tactical-load window depending on recovery.
rules.MD_minus_2: Moderate tactical and reduced neuromuscular load.
rules.MD_minus_1: Activation, set pieces, low-volume accelerations, and clarity.
rules.MD: Warm-up, match, and post-match exposure log.

backend_records_to_create.name: Match-day-minus exercise placement
backend_records_to_create.summary: Place high-soreness strength, dense COD, and demanding conditioning away from match day; use low-volume activation near match day.

rules.heavy_strength: Prefer MD-4 or MD-3 in normal weeks.
rules.max_velocity: Use small controlled exposure early or midweek; avoid new volume on MD-1.
rules.deceleration_cod: Main load earlier than MD-2 unless volume is very low.
rules.conditioning: Match the method to adaptation and calendar.
rules.activation: Use MD-1 for mobility, low-volume speed touches, and tactical rehearsal.

backend_records_to_create.name: Congested fixture adjustment
backend_records_to_create.summary: When fixtures are close together, prioritize availability and performance with recovery, microdoses, squad splitting, and medical/readiness checks.

rules.starters: Recovery, tactical clarity, mobility, short activation, and symptom checks.
rules.partial_minutes: Top-up only the missed qualities that matter for the player's role.
rules.non_starters: Controlled conditioning and strength if next-match role allows.
rules.returning_players: Avoid first full match exposure during congested windows when possible.

backend_records_to_create.name: Preseason speed and tissue-capacity ramp
backend_records_to_create.summary: Preseason should rebuild sprint, HIR, COD, strength, and tissue capacity gradually before full match density.

rules.week_1: Movement quality, aerobic re-entry, low-volume accelerations, basic strength, and injury-history screening.
rules.week_2_to_3: Progress high-speed exposure, COD, unilateral strength, and small-sided density.
rules.week_4_plus: Increase match-specific exposure and tactical fitness while avoiding abrupt spikes.

backend_records_to_create.name: General return-to-play continuum
backend_records_to_create.summary: Progress from return to participation to return to sport and then return to performance.
phase_gates: strength and range restored enough for phase

backend_records_to_create.name: Return-to-run progression
backend_records_to_create.summary: Progress linear running before high-intensity, sprinting, COD, and football-specific actions.

backend_records_to_create.name: Hamstring RTP rule
backend_records_to_create.summary: Hamstring RTP should restore sprint mechanics, eccentric strength, high-speed exposure, and position-specific match running before full return.
position_notes: wide players and forwards need open-field sprint exposure
center backs need recovery sprint exposure

backend_records_to_create.name: Groin and adductor RTP rule
backend_records_to_create.summary: Groin RTP should restore adductor strength, cutting, lateral push-off, kicking, and position-specific football volume.
phase_gates: Copenhagen or adductor strength progression tolerated

backend_records_to_create.name: ACL and major knee RTP rule
backend_records_to_create.summary: Knee RTP should be criteria based and include strength, hop, landing, COD, psychological readiness, football contact, and minutes progression.

backend_records_to_create.name: Ankle, calf, and Achilles RTP rule
backend_records_to_create.summary: Ankle/calf/Achilles RTP should restore calf strength, balance, hop capacity, tendon response, sprinting, and COD before full play.
phase_gates: football training and match minutes tolerated

backend_records_to_create.name: Football readiness traffic light
backend_records_to_create.summary: Classify readiness before high-risk sessions as green, amber, or red.
backend_records_to_create.green: Normal soreness, no escalating pain, good recovery, no red flags; proceed as planned.
backend_records_to_create.amber: Low sleep, high soreness, minor symptoms, recent load spike, or congestion; reduce load, intensity, or risky elements.
backend_records_to_create.red: Acute injury, suspected concussion, swelling, instability, severe pain, neurological symptoms, or worsening tendon/muscle symptoms; stop and refer.

backend_records_to_create.name: Match minutes and exposure adjustment
backend_records_to_create.summary: Adjust next-session load based on minutes, position, and actual exposure rather than squad-wide assumptions.

rules.starter_high_minutes: Prioritize recovery and tissue check before extra load.
rules.partial_minutes: Top up only missing qualities if next-match schedule allows.
rules.unused_sub: Use role-specific top-up running, speed, strength, and tactical work.
rules.returning_player: Limit minutes progression and monitor next-day response.

backend_records_to_create.name: Low chronic load and return-from-break adjustment
backend_records_to_create.summary: Players returning from break, illness, or low exposure need gradual progression before match-like speed, COD, and minutes.

rules.first_week_back: Limit maximal sprint/COD and build movement quality.
rules.second_week_back: Increase high-speed, strength, and tactical density if symptoms and soreness allow.
rules.before_full_match: Confirm exposure to position-specific speed, braking, and conditioning.

backend_records_to_create.name: Body-region symptom adjustment
backend_records_to_create.summary: Modify session content based on the body region that is symptomatic.

rules.hamstring: Reduce max sprinting and long high-speed runs; keep tolerable isometrics/strength and graded running under guidance.
rules.groin: Reduce lateral cutting and kicking volume; use tolerable adductor isometrics.
rules.knee: Reduce jumping, deep cutting, and contact if swelling or instability exists; refer if acute.
rules.ankle: Reduce chaotic COD and jumping; emphasize balance and controlled hop progressions.
rules.calf_achilles: Reduce sprinting, plyometrics, and hard-surface volume; monitor morning response.

backend_records_to_create.name: Youth growth-spurt adjustment
backend_records_to_create.summary: If rapid growth, coordination drop, or new growth-related pain is present, lower peak load and protect movement quality.

rules.load_response: Reduce high-impact, sprint, and COD volume temporarily.
rules.training_focus: Keep strength technique, mobility, balance, and low-symptom football skill.
rules.medical_flag: Persistent heel, knee, hip, groin, or back pain should prompt clinical review.

backend_records_to_create.name: Surface and footwear change adjustment
backend_records_to_create.summary: Reduce novel sprint, COD, and plyometric load when surface or footwear changes substantially.

rules.harder_surface: Watch calf, Achilles, shin, and foot response.
rules.slippery_surface: Reduce maximal COD and open chaotic play if slipping is common.
rules.new_boots: Avoid pairing new boots with high-volume sprint/COD sessions.
